o1.biggest_strength: Every email serves one of the two habits that predict retention, and email 5 targets whichever habit each user is still missing, using only triggers the tool supports, with skip rules and platform branching.
o1.biggest_mistake: The control group gets no onboarding emails at all, which risks losing users. Email 5 also needs two versions with different buttons, which adds build work.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Compare the new series against a holdout on the old series, and give each email a numeric 'worked if' target the way the welcome email has one.

o2.biggest_strength: The copy is clean and ready to paste. Each email has a clear 'worked if' number, the inactivity email is guilt-free, and the drop list links back to the customers' own words.
o2.biggest_mistake: It spends the fifth email on Pro instead of pushing users to the habit they haven't formed yet. That weakens the focus on the 67% both-habits group, and the claim about what Pro reminders do needs checking.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the Pro email with a 'missing habit' email and send Pro after day 30 to active users.

reason: Both are calm, on-brand and branch by platform. Output 1 keeps all five emails on the two habits that drive retention and saves Pro until users are hooked, which is the series I'd rather run.
